# task-e452cd61: recolor the empty continuation beyond a truncated stripe

## Trigger and validated behavior
Use when a solid background contains a full-length straight stripe of one color, plus a second stripe row/column of the same color that stops short at an edge. The demonstrated behavior extends/recolors the empty continuation of the shorter stripe out to the boundary using color 1, while leaving the stripe's existing cells unchanged.

## Evidence
Demo 1 (10x28): background 3; one full horizontal stripe of 5 at row 1, and another full horizontal stripe at row 5 except the far-right cell is background 3. Output changes only that final cell (row 1-indexed 2, column 1-indexed 28) from 3 to 1.

Demo 2 (29x14): background 8, with a repeated 4x10 pattern made of 0 and 8 in rows 0–3, 11–14, and 21–24 (zero-indexed). In every pattern block, the same row has a 0-pattern followed by trailing background 8's at columns 11–13. Output changes precisely those trailing cells (all 3 columns in each of the three matching rows) to 1, preserving pattern cells and all other background.

Test task-e452cd61 (29x27): background 9, full horizontal stripe color 7 at row 3, second horizontal stripe at row 21 from columns 0–16, with background 9 in columns 17–26. Correct output keeps the 7s and extends the remainder of that second stripe through the right edge in color 1. The accepted output had row 21 (zero-based) `[7]*17 + [1]*10`; all other cells unchanged.

## Rule notes
- The second, truncated band/line has an endpoint at the grid edge followed by a uniform-background gap along its row/column; recolor the missing continuation in 1, not the stripe's original color.
- Demo 2 reveals repeated templates can contain multiple separate occurrences: apply continuation to every corresponding row in each repeated block, not just the first occurrence.
- In Demo 2, continuation begins after column 10, not immediately after the distinctive zeros; specifically the extent/orientation is inherited from the stripe run in the row.
- Preserve full stripes and every non-target cell. Re-identify background, line color, orientation, truncated line, and target span per instance rather than hard-coding positions/colors.

## Caution / prior wrong submissions
On the validated test, initial malformed submission had one `1` embedded at the end of the shortened 7 stripe while leaving the rest of the intended continuation as background; that grid was rejected as invalid because one row had only 26 cells. The next valid 29x27 attempt made only the first missing cell color 1 (column 17 zero-indexed), leaving the rest background, and was incorrect. Extend the whole missing segment to the boundary in 1. Thus the continuation includes all cells after the truncated stripe endpoint, not merely the adjacent one."
}
